impDef.description: Whether or not an exception condition is raised when the target TYPE in an iterate call indicates CHARACTER or CHARACTER LARGE OBJECT and the source value is a zero-length character string.
Whether the invocation of a foreign-data wrapper interface function is supported or the invocation of a foreign-data wrapper interface procedure.
Whether the foreign-data wrapper interface routines of a given SQL-implementation are either all functions or all procedures.

The effect when the value of any input argument provided by the caller of a foreign-data wrapper interface routine falls outside the set of allowed values of the data type of the parameter, or when the value of any output argument resulting from the execution of the foreign-data wrapper interface routine falls outside the set of values supported by the caller of a foreign-data wrapper interface routine for that parameter.
The implementation-defined rules that cause exception conditions to be raised when a foreign-data wrapper interface routine does not execute successfully.
The affect on a foreign table descriptor, apart from its generic options descriptor when alter generic options is specified.
Whether implementation-defined foreign-data wrapper descriptor fields are retrievable.
Whether implementation-defined foreign-data wrapper descriptor fields are settable.
The reasons why the resources to manage a query context cannot be allocated.
The reasons why the resources to manage a foreign-data wrapper environment cannot be allocated.
The reasons why the resources to manage a foreign-server connection cannot be allocated.
The way in which the foreign-data wrapper knows the URI to specify in the XML document.
The reasons why the resources to manage a foreign-data wrapper reply cannot be allocated.
The reasons why the resources to manage a foreign-data wrapper execution cannot be allocated.
The reasons why the resources to manage a foreign-data descriptor area cannot be allocated.

The subclass code which is generated when the routine’s return code indicates No data found, and no status record is generated corresponding to SQLSTATE value '02000' but there may be status records generated corresponding to SQLSTATE value '02nnn', where 'nnn' is the subclass code.
The exception condition raised when the resources to manage a query context cannot be allocated for reasons not specified by ISO/IEC 9075.
The exception condition raised when the resources to manage a foreign-data wrapper environment cannot be allocated for reasons not specified by ISO/IEC 9075.
The exception condition raised when the resources to manage a foreign-server connection cannot be allocated for reasons not specified by ISO/IEC 9075.
The exception condition raised when the resources to manage a foreign-data wrapper reply cannot be allocated for reasons not specified by ISO/IEC 9075.
The exception condition raised when the resources to manage a foreign-data wrapper execution cannot be allocated for reasons not specified by ISO/IEC 9075.
The exception condition is raised when the resources to manage a foreign-data descriptor area cannot be allocated for reasons not specified by ISO/IEC 9075.
The nullability characteristic and the default option of each column specified by a basic column definition when a basic column definition list of a foreign table definition is specified.
The column descriptors included in a foreign table descriptor when a basic column definition list of a foreign table definition is not specified.
The nullability characteristic and default option included in the column descriptor specified by a basic column definition.
The default value for the precision of the NUMERIC data type.
The default value for the precision of the DECIMAL data type.
Any implementation-defined data types.
Any additional requirements for the result of evaluating a data location in a datalink value constructor.
Any additional privileges necessary to execute a foreign table definition.
Any additional privileges necessary to execute a user mapping definition.
Any additional requirements for the validity of the Write Token for an Update via a datalink.
Any additional privileges necessary to execute a foreign server definition.
Any additional privileges necessary to execute a routine mapping definition.
The maximum length of an identifier.
The maximum length of a variable-length character string type.

The maximum datalink length determined by the amount of space, in octets, that is allocated for, a host variable of data type DATALINK, an argument of declared type DATALINK to an invocation of an external routine, the value returned by an invocation of an external function whose result type is DATALINK. The maximum datalink length constrains the values of expressions whose declared type is DATALINK such that every such value can be assigned to a host variable, substituted for a parameter to an external routine, or returned by an invocation of an external function.
The maximum lengths of foreign-data wrapper diagnostics area fields whose data types are CHARACTER VARYING.
The maximum length of the variable-length character string of the result of a url complete expression.
The maximum length of the variable-length character string of the result of a url path expression.

The maximum length of the variable-length character string of the result of a url complete only expression.
The maximum length of the variable-length character string of the result of a url path for write expression.
The maximum lengths of foreign-data wrapper item descriptor fields whose data type is CHARACTER VARYING.
The maximum length of datalink attributes whose data type is CHARACTER VARYING.
The maximum number of foreign-data wrapper environments.
The maximum number of foreign-server connections.
The maximum number of foreign-data wrapper replies.

Header fields and item fields in foreign-data wrapper descriptor areas.
The SQL-statement codes assigned to SQL-statements that are defined by a foreign-data wrapper.
